newsitem.title: UK: Sinn Fein seeks British reply to peace formula.
newsitem.headline: Sinn Fein seeks British reply to peace formula.

text.p: The Irish Republican Army's political wing stepped up demands on Saturday for Britain to reply to Northern Irish peace feelers, saying London held the key to lasting calm.

As Sinn Fein activists met in the Irish Republic to review a peace drive shattered by guerrilla bombs, a senior official said Sinn Fein would "move heaven and earth" to get an IRA ceasefire if Britain agreed a new formula to break a political stalemate.
Martin McGuinness said Britain had had proposals from moderate nationalist leader John Hume and Sinn Fein leader Gerry Adams for more than a month but not yet responded.

Challenging Britain to be "a driving-force for change," Sinn Fein chief strategist McGuinness told reporters before the conference in Athboy, County Meath: "We need an urgent process of credible peace negotations.
"We need those...to take place against the background of a peaceful environment, and we are working night and day every day of the week to try and achieve that."
Adams told reporters: "What we need now is courage from (British Prime Minister John) Major. The key is in his hands."

A one-day conference of several hundred Sinn Fein members was held in a climate of uncertainty about a peace process that collapsed in February when the IRA set off bombs in London protesting a British refusal to allow Sinn Fein into talks.

Security chiefs in Britain have warned the IRA could strike again at any time. On Thursday a dissident republican group tried to blow up a police base in Londonderry city. A 600 lb car bomb was defused.

The Irish Times newspaper reported that Sinn Fein delegates would be given a report of a recent secret meeting of IRA commanders who reportedly backed Sinn Fein's demand for inclusion in political talks and set out terms for truce.
Sinn Fein sources denied the newspaper report and said the conference would discuss "conflict resolution processes".

Republican sources say the IRA will not reinstate a truce unless Britain signals that Sinn Fein will get a place in time-limited all-party talks that will not be stymied by rows over demands for an early surrender of guerrilla weapons.

A British government spokesman said on Saturday that its position had not changed. "We believe that should there be a ceasefire (which) should be absolutely unequivocal...That must be the case before Sinn Fein may join talks."
Hume, leader of the Social Democratic and Labour Party, who put a formula to Major after talking to Adams, declines to specify its terms.
But he said his proposals are geared towards providing "reassurances" about the nature of all-party talks and the comprehensiveness of an agenda for them.
He says he is convinced the IRA will call a truce if Major responds positively.
But British Conservative Party MP Andrew Hunter, who specialises in Northern Ireland affairs, did not share Hume's optimism.

"I think John Hume is suffering from a form of amnesia because it was he a year ago who coined the phrase "You can't negotiate with people with guns on the table, guns under the table or outside the door' and that is precisely the position," he told BBC radio.
Unionist politicians speaking for majority Protestants who say they will not let the IRA bomb them into an all-Ireland state, were suspicious of McGuinness's comments.

"I have no doubt that if the prime minister were to cave into the IRA's demands, they would call a ceasefire. But (that) would be unacceptable to the Unionist community," Democratic Unionist Party deputy leader Peter Robinson told Reuters.
